title: Question words
goal: Ask where, when, how, why, how much, who and what, in informal, neutral and formal French.

items.note: With an accent, où = where. Without it, ou = or.

example.fr: Comment est-ce que tu vas au travail ? — En bus.
example.en: How do you get to work? — By bus.

items.note: Before a vowel: parce qu'il, parce qu'elle, parce qu'on.

example.en: How many children do you have?

items.note: Before a noun, add de (d'): combien de personnes, combien d'enfants.

items.en: what (at the end of an informal question)
items.note: At the start of a question, use qu'est-ce que instead.

items.en: which / what + noun (agrees with the noun)

drills.prompt: Complete: ___ sports est-ce que tu aimes ?
drills.explain: le sport is masculine; sports is plural → quels.

items.fr: Tu vas où ? / Où est-ce que tu vas ? / Où vas-tu ?
items.en: three ways to ask a question: informal, neutral, formal

drills.prompt: Where do you work? (to a friend)
drills.explain: All four are correct; the first two are everyday speech, est-ce que is neutral, inversion is formal.
finir → vous finissez. Inversion: Quand finissez-vous ?
Inversion puts the verb before the subject, joined by a hyphen: habitez-vous.

steps.title: Twenty questions at the language café

blocks.title: A language café in Gatineau
blocks.context: Karim and Sofia take French classes at the same community centre. They meet at the Thursday café.

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.en: Karim. Where are you from, Sofia?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Je suis mexicaine. Mais maintenant, j'habite ici, à Gatineau.
lines.en: I'm Mexican. But now I live here, in Gatineau.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Parce que mon mari travaille à Ottawa. Et toi, tu habites où ?
lines.en: Because my husband works in Ottawa. And you, where do you live?

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.fr: À Gatineau aussi. Quand est-ce que tu as ton cours de français ?
lines.en: In Gatineau too. When do you have your French class?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Le mardi et le jeudi soir. Il y a combien d'étudiants dans ton cours ?
lines.en: Tuesday and Thursday evenings. How many students are there in your class?

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.fr: Douze. Et qui est ton prof ?
lines.en: Twelve. And who is your teacher?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: C'est Lucie. Elle est super ! Tu parles quelle langue à la maison ?
lines.en: It's Lucie. She's great! Which language do you speak at home?

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.fr: L'arabe et le français. Quel est ton numéro ? On pratique ensemble ?
lines.en: Arabic and French. What's your number? Shall we practise together?

blocks.body: Listen first. Count the questions: how many different question words can you hear?

blocks.title: The question words
head: Question word
English
Example
blocks.note: [[Pourquoi]] asks “why”; you answer with [[parce que]] (“because”). Before a vowel it becomes [[parce qu']]: [[parce qu'il fait froid]].

blocks.title: One question, three registers
blocks.pattern: Tu vas où ? · Où est-ce que tu vas ? · Où vas-tu ?
blocks.note:
- **Informal (speaking with friends):** keep the normal word order and put the question word at the end or at the start: [[Tu vas où ?]] or [[Où tu vas ?]]
- **Neutral (fine everywhere):** question word + [[est-ce que]] + normal order: [[Où est-ce que tu vas ?]]
- **Formal (writing, polite situations):** question word + verb-subject, with a hyphen: [[Où vas-tu ?]] [[Où allez-vous ?]]

All three mean exactly the same thing. Learn to **understand** all three and to **use** at least the neutral one everywhere.

examples.fr: Vous travaillez où ? / Où est-ce que vous travaillez ? / Où travaillez-vous ?
Tu finis quand ? / Quand est-ce que tu finis ? / Quand finis-tu ?
Ça coûte combien ? / Combien est-ce que ça coûte ? / Combien coûte le billet ?
examples.en: How much does it (the ticket) cost?

examples.fr: Tu fais quoi ? / Qu'est-ce que tu fais ? / Que fais-tu ?

blocks.title: Quoi, qu'est-ce que, que
blocks.body:
“What” changes form depending on where it sits:

- At the **end** of an informal question: [[quoi]] → [[Tu manges quoi ?]]
- At the **start**, neutral: [[qu'est-ce que]] → [[Qu'est-ce que tu manges ?]]
- At the start, formal inversion: [[que]] → [[Que manges-tu ?]]

Never start a full question with *quoi*: [[Quoi tu manges ?]] is wrong (fixed phrases like [[Quoi de neuf ?]] are the exception). [[Quoi ?]] on its own means “What?” (a bit abrupt; [[Pardon ?]] is more polite).

blocks.title: Quel agrees with its noun
head: singular
plural
blocks.note:
[[Quel]] goes **directly before a noun**, or before [[est]] / [[sont]] + noun: [[Quel jour ?]] [[Quelle est ton adresse ?]] [[Quels sports ?]] [[Quelles langues ?]]

Good news: all four forms sound the same. You only hear a difference in the plural before a vowel: [[quelles‿activités]] (a *z* sound).

blocks.title: Words and phrases in this lesson

blocks.body:
- **où or ou?** [[où]] (accent) = where; [[ou]] (no accent) = or. [[Tu habites où ?]] but [[du thé ou du café ?]]
- **“What is your…?”** uses [[quel]], not *qu'est-ce que*: [[Quel est ton nom ?]] — never *Qu'est-ce que est ton nom ?*
- **combien de + noun, no article:** [[combien d'enfants]], not *combien des enfants*.
- **Inversion needs a hyphen:** [[Où vas-tu ?]] With *il/elle* and a verb ending in a vowel, add **-t-** for the sound: [[Où travaille-t-elle ?]] [[Où va-t-il ?]]
- **pourquoi vs pour quoi:** one word = why. Two words = “for what”.

- [[Quand est-ce que]]: the silent *d* of *quand* comes back as a **t** sound: *kan-tess-kuh*.
- [[Comment allez-vous ?]]: the *t* links too: *ko-man-ta-lay-voo*.
- [[parce que]] is said in two short beats: *pars-kuh*.
- [[pourquoi]]: *poor-kwa*. [[combien]]: *kom-byan*, with nasal vowels and no final *n* sound.
- In informal questions the question word carries the stress: [[Tu vas **où** ?]]

In everyday Québec French the informal pattern is by far the most common: [[Tu travailles où ?]] [[Ça coûte combien ?]] Inversion sounds formal or written.

Two things you will hear:

- [[rester]] often means **to live**: [[Je reste à Laval]] = I live in Laval. [[Tu restes où ?]] = Where do you live?
- A little question word [[-tu]] after the verb in very relaxed speech: [[C'est-tu loin ?]] (Is it far?). Just **recognize** it; don't use it in an exam.

examples.en: Where do you live? — In Laval. (Québec)

blocks.prompt: At a language café, interview a new classmate. Ask at least five questions with five different question words, then answer one “why” question yourself with parce que.

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut ! Tu t'appelles comment ? Tu es d'où ? Tu habites où maintenant ? Quand est-ce que tu as ton cours de français ? Tu parles quelles langues ? Et pourquoi tu apprends le français ? Moi, j'apprends le français parce que je travaille à Montréal.
models.en: Hi! What's your name? Where are you from? Where do you live now? When do you have your French class? Which languages do you speak? And why are you learning French? I'm learning French because I work in Montréal.

blocks.prompt: Write a short note to a new neighbour. Introduce yourself in one sentence, then ask four polite questions with vous (use inversion or est-ce que).
checklist: At least two different question words

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Raj, j'habite dans l'appartement 12. Comment vous appelez-vous ? Où travaillez-vous ? Quelles langues est-ce que vous parlez ? Est-ce que vous avez des enfants ? Mes enfants ont huit et dix ans.
models.en: Hello! My name is Raj, I live in apartment 12. What's your name? Where do you work? Which languages do you speak? Do you have children? My children are eight and ten.

summary:
- Ask questions with [[où, quand, comment, pourquoi, combien (de), qui, quoi]] and answer *why* with [[parce que]]
- Make [[quel / quelle / quels / quelles]] agree with the noun
- Ask the same question three ways: [[Tu vas où ?]] [[Où est-ce que tu vas ?]] [[Où vas-tu ?]]
